claims.statement: The deck states that 117 million mobile users in Tanzania equal 117 million potential Pesalo customers
claims.limitations: Establishes what the deck claims, not its truth

claims.units_denominator: Subscriptions (SIMs used at least once in 90 days, plus fixed lines)

confidence.reason: Regulator's administrative data for exactly this measure

market_applicability.scope: United Republic of Tanzania, telecom subscriptions (not people)

claims.limitations: Subscriptions, not unique people or households

claims.statement: TCRA defines a subscription as a SIM used at least once for voice, SMS or data in the past 90 days, and reports penetration of 167.0% (telecom) and 89.7% (internet) without stating the population denominator.

basis.locator: Glossary p.7-8; snapshot p.10; Figure 1.1.4.1 p.17; p.35

confidence.reason: Definitions and figures read directly from the report

claims.limitations: Denominator not stated; implied denominator is an inference, not a reported figure

confidence.reason: Authoritative compiler but a modelled estimate between censuses

market_applicability.scope: United Republic of Tanzania, total population

claims.limitations: Estimate; compare with NBS projections when precision matters

claims.statement: Telecom subscription counts cannot be read as unique people or audience reach: end-June 2026 subscriptions (about 117.0 million) exceed the estimated 2025 total population (about 70.5 million) of all ages.

basis.reasoning: A count larger than the whole population must include multiple subscriptions per person and non-person subscriptions (machine-to-machine SIMs are reported separately); the 90-day activity definition also counts intermittently used SIMs.

confidence.reason: Follows arithmetically from two direct measures and the stated definition

market_applicability.reason: Based on local regulator and population data

claims.limitations: Does not estimate the number of unique mobile users; that requires survey or operator unique-user data
claims.review_condition: When either input record is superseded

basis.calculation: 210,000 / 1,400,000 = 15.0%; 30-day retention as reported in Appendix A

hypotheses.proposition: Failed cash-outs, driven by agent float shortages, are a major cause of Pesalo's early churn
hypotheses.basis: High cash-out failure rate, low retention and review complaints
hypotheses.confirming_signal: 30-day retention markedly lower for users whose first cash-out failed than for those whose first cash-out succeeded
hypotheses.falsifier: Similar retention regardless of first cash-out outcome
hypotheses.decision_impact: If true, reliability fixes should come before acquisition spend
hypotheses.validation_step: Cohort analysis of Q2 registrants by first cash-out outcome (first-party data, days not months)

confidence.reason: Pattern plausible and consistent, but the link to churn has not been measured

hypotheses.confirming_signal: Higher sign-ups in radio regions than matched holdout regions in the same weeks
hypotheses.falsifier: No difference in a regional holdout test
hypotheses.decision_impact: Determines whether radio deserves acquisition budget
hypotheses.validation_step: Regional holdout test once retention is fixed

confidence.reason: Observational association confounded by salary timing

hypotheses.proposition: Young Tanzanians want savings to feel like a game and reject banks
hypotheses.basis: Deck slide 4 assertion; no research cited
hypotheses.confirming_signal: Research with target users showing gamified saving increases saving behaviour
hypotheses.falsifier: Research showing reliability, fees or access matter more
hypotheses.validation_step: Switching interviews with active and lapsed savers

hypotheses.proposition: 100,000 users will pay TZS 5,000 a month for Pesalo Gold in year one
hypotheses.confirming_signal: Priced test conversion consistent with target
hypotheses.falsifier: Low conversion in a priced test
hypotheses.decision_impact: Drives part of the budget request
hypotheses.validation_step: Priced test with existing active savers

confidence.reason: No willingness-to-pay evidence; the target equals almost half of current monthly active users

insights.audience_context: New Pesalo users in their first 30 days
insights.observation: Most new users stop transacting within a month, cash-out failures are frequent, and failed withdrawals dominate one-star reviews
insights.contrast: Acquisition ambition in the deck versus retention and reliability in the appendix
insights.mechanism: Users who cannot withdraw their savings when needed lose trust and stop using the wallet, so acquisition spend buys churn
insights.explanation: Pesalo's growth problem looks like a leaking bucket rather than a shortage of sign-ups
alternatives: Users sign up for a one-off purpose and never intended to save
Fees or app crashes drive churn more than cash-out failures
contradictions: Crashes and fees also appear in reviews (22 and 17 of 120)

confidence.reason: Consistent signals, but the churn link is not yet measured by cohort

insights.implication: Fund reliability and onboarding before scaled acquisition; measure the churn link first

options.title: Deck proposal: viral Gen Z campaign plus Pesalo Gold (TZS 2.5 billion)
options.diagnosis_addressed: Assumed shortage of awareness and sign-ups among young users
options.where_to_act: Gen Z nationally via TikTok and influencers
options.how_to_win: Viral challenge, gamified savings, premium subscription
options.economics: unknown: no unit economics, retention-adjusted acquisition cost or subscription conversion evidence in the deck
options.rationale: Rests on misread market size, unsourced psychology, a Kenyan proxy and a confounded radio claim, while the appendix shows a retention and reliability problem

options.title: Fix the leaking bucket first: cash-out reliability and onboarding, measure the churn link, then gated acquisition
options.diagnosis_addressed: Low retention with frequent cash-out failures (INS-C01)
options.where_to_act: Top agents and new users' first 30 days
options.how_to_win: Make the first save-and-withdraw experience reliable, then acquire where reliability is proven

mechanism.explanation: Higher retention raises the value of every acquired user and lowers effective acquisition cost

options.economics: Float partner cost unknown: quote needed. Value depends on retention gain; cohort analysis will size it. Acquisition budget released only after retention improves
options.resources: Operations and product time; float partner fee; a small part of the TZS 2.5 billion request
risks: Cash-out failures are not the main churn driver
non_choices: No viral influencer campaign in H1 2027
No Pesalo Gold launch before a priced test
No national radio expansion before a holdout test
conditions: Cohort analysis shows materially lower retention after a failed first cash-out; otherwise re-diagnose churn
Acquisition spend released only when 30-day retention of new users exceeds an agreed threshold
reversal_triggers: No retention difference by first cash-out outcome: re-diagnose (fees, crashes, purpose of sign-up)
options.rationale: Keeps the deck's sound operational fix, addresses the evident retention constraint and makes acquisition spend conditional on evidence

options.title: Pesalo Gold subscription
options.economics: unknown: willingness to pay not measured
conditions: Priced test among active savers before any launch decision
reversal_triggers: Test conversion far below the level needed to cover costs
options.rationale: No willingness-to-pay evidence; revisit after the retention fix

metrics.decision_rule: Flat active savers after two quarters: re-diagnose

defects.claim_or_section: Slide 2: 117 million mobile users = 117 million potential customers
defects.defect: Subscriptions are presented as people and as addressable customers
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: TCRA counts about 117.0 million subscriptions (SIMs active in 90 days, incl. machine-to-machine) against a population of about 70.5 million of all ages (CLM-TZ-004, CLM-TZ-006, CLM-TZ-007)
defects.strategic_consequence: Market size overstated many times over; targets and budget built on it are unfounded
defects.required_fix: Size the market with unique adults with mobile money access in target areas, from survey data, and state the scope
defects.retest_condition: Market size built from a people-based source with scope and date

defects.defect: A SWOT list replaces diagnosis and choice; 'leverage strengths to capture opportunities' excludes nothing
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: No diagnosis or trade-offs in the deck
defects.strategic_consequence: No basis for allocating the budget
defects.required_fix: State the diagnosis (retention and reliability), the guiding choice and non-choices
defects.retest_condition: Storyline contains a diagnosis, a choice and explicit non-choices

defects.claim_or_section: Slide 4: Gen Z crave instant gratification and hate banks
defects.defect: Invented psychology and a demographic stereotype used as an insight
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: No research cited; appendix and reviews point to reliability, not gamification (CLM-C04)
defects.strategic_consequence: Product and campaign built on an unsupported motive
defects.required_fix: Remove; replace with a hypothesis to test through switching interviews with active and lapsed savers

defects.claim_or_section: Slide 5: Kenyan youth adoption proves Tanzania will follow
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: Report not supplied; Kenyan scope; no Tanzanian adoption evidence (CLM-C06)
defects.required_fix: Remove as proof; if relevant, list as a hypothesis with a local validation step
defects.retest_condition: Tanzanian evidence on savings app adoption

defects.defect: Generic positioning that any competitor could use
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: Competitor substitution test fails; no proof point
defects.strategic_consequence: No distinctive reason to choose or trust Pesalo
defects.required_fix: Defer positioning until the reliability promise can be proven; then test a reliability-based proposition
defects.retest_condition: Proposition with proof, tested with target users

defects.claim_or_section: Slide 7: Pesalo Gold, 100,000 subscribers at TZS 5,000 a month
defects.defect: Premium subscription target without willingness-to-pay evidence; the target is almost half of current monthly active users
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: No pricing research or test; 210,000 monthly active users (CLM-C02)
defects.strategic_consequence: Revenue plan and budget request overstated
defects.required_fix: Priced test with active savers before any launch decision
defects.retest_condition: Test conversion and retention of subscribers

defects.claim_or_section: Slide 8: viral TikTok challenge, 10 million views
defects.defect: Virality treated as the strategy before the business problem and communications task are established
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: Appendix shows 22% 30-day retention; no evidence awareness is the constraint
defects.required_fix: Hold acquisition campaigns until retention improves; define the communications task afterwards
defects.retest_condition: Retention above agreed threshold and a defined communications task

defects.defect: Correlation presented as causal ROI; radio weeks coincided with salary weeks
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: Five of eight radio weeks were salary weeks; stratified differences 5-9% on tiny numbers of weeks (CLM-C05)
defects.strategic_consequence: Media budget justified by a confounded association
defects.required_fix: State as unproven; run a regional holdout test

defects.defect: Exposure and vanity metrics only; no retention, active savers or unit economics
defects.strategic_consequence: Success could be declared while the business loses users
defects.required_fix: Measure cash-out success, cohort retention, active savers and acquisition cost per retained saver
defects.retest_condition: Measurement plan includes behavioural and business outcomes with decision rules

defects.claim_or_section: Deck overall: acquisition strategy ignores the appendix
defects.defect: The deck's own data show a retention and reliability constraint that the strategy does not address
defects.evidence_or_missing_evidence: 15% of registered accounts active; 22% 30-day retention; 18% cash-out failures (CLM-C02, CLM-C03)
defects.strategic_consequence: TZS 2.5 billion would be spent filling a leaking bucket
defects.required_fix: Rebuild around reliability and retention; make acquisition conditional
defects.retest_condition: Storyline leads with retention diagnosis and conditional acquisition

gate_results.reason: Virality and Gen Z ambition treated as the strategy; business constraint not diagnosed
Key claims unsourced or misread; appendix contradicts strategy
Confounded radio association presented as ROI
SWOT instead of choice; no non-choices
No unit economics; subscription target unsupported
No competitor data in the deck
Subscriptions as people; Kenyan proxy as proof
The one operational action (float partner) is feasible and addresses a measured problem
Slides are clear but argue for the wrong problem
